subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards add an explicit append, segment, or adaptive mode for long replies, or should maintainers keep only full-content CardKit streaming with stronger coalescing?
rationale: Current source and history show full-content updates are intentional to prevent truncation, but the issue and fresh live repro show unacceptable latency for some deployments and dispute whether the open coalescing pull request is enough.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded opt-in mode
options.body: Add a documented Feishu-owned opt-in append, segment, or adaptive mode with tests and live proof while keeping full-content CardKit streaming as the default.

options.title: Continue coalescing-only review
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91943 as the only fix path, but require live timing proof that it materially improves long replies.

options.title: Reject alternate modes for now
options.body: Keep only the documented full-content CardKit contract and ask affected deployments to disable streaming or use a separate plugin fork until stronger data exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded opt-in mode
recommendation.body: Add a documented Feishu-owned opt-in append, segment, or adaptive mode with tests and live proof while keeping full-content CardKit streaming as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: The package declares this handle as the Feishu community maintainer, so they are the best available owner for a Feishu channel behavior and compatibility choice.
